edits.after: A simple with epsilon_i=0 would have only the word i^c j, since there is only one j and any other position of j leaves a terminal i. For c>=a+1 multiply the native projective Serre relation on the LEFT by P_(i,c-a-1) and pair with this simple. Every s>0 term has a terminal i^s block and its actual word corner is zero. The s=0 term has the nonzero defining i^c j corner; the tensor product of the divided nil-Hecke idempotents on its consecutive i-blocks is full and therefore detects it. This gives one nonzero positive Laurent polynomial equal to zero, a contradiction. Equivalently these are exact divided restriction/G_0 operators; no simple-socle crystal operator is substituted into a Serre sum.

edits.before: No Ind(U,C) has this corner: C has no first i, and because A has no terminal i or j, the strict smaller-i-tail character of U forces a color outside {i,j} after the original A boundary in every shuffle attempting that corner.
edits.after: No Ind(U,C) has this defining corner. Every word of A ends in a color outside {i,j}; in any shuffle producing U from Ind(A,L_b), all original A i/j letters occur before A's final outside-color letter, since their order is preserved. In the target defining A|i^b|C word, the prefix through that final outside-color letter contains exactly the original A i/j counts. Thus no j from C can occur in that prefix: it would increase the j count, and no original A j can move past that final letter to compensate. Nor can an added i from C or from the L_b block occur there, by the identical i-count argument. The following i^b block cannot get an i from C, because C has first-i tail0, so every nonempty word of C starts in j; its preceding j can enter neither the prefix just counted nor the pure i^b block. Hence all b consecutive i after the final outside-color letter must come from U, giving a terminal i-tail of length at least b in U, contrary to epsilon_i(U)<b. If C is the vacuum the same conclusion is immediate. This is the actual count/ordering exclusion, rather than an inference from the smaller-epsilon inequality alone.

supplier_contracts.exact_statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $K_0(R):=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}K_0(R(\beta))$ be the split Grothendieck group of finite graded projective modules with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$ ([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]], [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]], [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]).
(i) The induction product $[P][P']:=[\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}(P\boxtimes P')]$ for $P\in K_0(R(\beta)),P'\in K_0(R(\gamma))$ makes $K_0(R)$ a unital associative $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebra, and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ makes it a coassociative counital $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-coalgebra; with the twisted multiplication on $K_0(R)\otimes K_0(R)$ defined by $(x_1\otimes x_2)(x_1'\otimes x_2')=q^{-(|x_2|\mid|x_1'|)}x_1x_1'\otimes x_2x_2'$ on homogeneous elements, $[\mathrm{Res}]$ is an algebra homomorphism ([[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]], KL I Propositions 3.1-3.2).
(ii) With the divided-power projectives $P_{i,n}$ of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], the classes $[P_{i,n}]$ satisfy, for all $i\ne j$, the divided-power quantum Serre relation
$$\sum_{a+b=-a_{ij}+1}(-1)^a[P_{i,a}]\,[P_{j,1}]\,[P_{i,b}]=0\qquad\text{in }K_0(R),$$
with the convention $[P_{i,0}]=1=[P_{j,0}]$, and satisfy $[P_{i,1}][P_{j,1}]=[P_{j,1}][P_{i,1}]$ when $a_{ij}=0$; these are the defining relations of the negative half.
(iii) Consequently the assignment $\theta_i\mapsto[P_{i,1}]$ extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism $\gamma:A f\to K_0(R)$ of the divided-power form of the negative half, with $\gamma(\theta_i^{(n)})=[P_{i,n}]$ and $\gamma(\theta_{i_1}^{(n_1)}\cdots\theta_{i_r}^{(n_r)})=[\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})]$; $\gamma$ is compatible with the coproducts ($r$ on $A f$ and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ on $K_0(R)$) and with the bar involutions, and it is $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear.

supplier_contracts.exact_statement:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$. Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is
$$e_{i,n}:=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\,\partial_{w_0}\in R(n\alpha_i),$$
and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift one has $R(n\alpha_i)\cong P_{i,n}^{\oplus[n]_{q_i}!}$ with $[n]_{q_i}!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^a-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$, so $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. For a divided-power sequence $\theta=i_1^{(n_1)}\cdots i_r^{(n_r)}$ put $\beta=\sum_an_a\alpha_{i_a}$ and $P_\theta:=\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})$ along the ordered concatenation of the blocks; then $[P_\theta]$ represents the ordered product of these divided powers; one may reorder only by the proved commuting/Serre relations, and adjacent colours need not commute, and for a single colour $\theta=i^{(n)}$ one has the indecomposability above.

supplier_contracts.exact_statement:
Let Q be the KLR datum above and beta,gamma in Q_+. Put A=R(beta+gamma), B=R(beta) tensor_k R(gamma), e=e(beta,gamma), and c=(beta|gamma). The bimodules eA and Ae are ungraded free respectively as left and right B-modules, of rank binomial(|beta|+|gamma|,|beta|). As GRADED modules they are finite projective direct sums of the appropriate principal idempotent B-modules with labelled shuffle shifts: for each concatenated word xi=nu*eta the right-module summand e(xi)B has shift delta_R(w,xi)=deg(tau_w e(xi)); the left-module summand B e(xi) has shift delta_L(w,xi)=deg(e(xi)tau_w)=delta_R(w,w^-1 xi), using respectively the corresponding right/left minimal shuffle representatives. These degrees depend on the labels; no common shift for an entire B copy is asserted. Ind=Ae tensor_B - and Res=e(-) are exact, commute with internal shifts, and preserve finitely generated graded projectives. Ind is left adjoint to Res. The right adjoint of Res is Coind=HOM_B(eA,-), with (a f)(t)=f(ta), and the exact generic second-adjunction formula is
Coind_(beta,gamma)(M boxtimes N) ~= Ind_(gamma,beta)(N boxtimes M){c}.
Thus the second adjunction reverses the two blocks and has the displayed shift; same-ordered unshifted biadjunction is not asserted. The formula is an isomorphism of functors and holds on arbitrary graded B-modules after interpreting the right side with the block-flip equivalence. This is distinct from the cyclotomic E_i/F_i biadjunction theorem. Moreover, e_(beta,gamma) R(beta+gamma) e_(beta',gamma') has a finite Mackey filtration indexed by nonnegative four-block weight matrices ((a,b),(c,d)) with row sums beta,gamma and column sums beta',gamma'. Its subquotient is the corresponding composite four-block restriction, flip of the middle blocks and induction bimodule, shifted by -(b|c). The same statement holds for arbitrary numbers of blocks.

supplier_contracts.exact_statement: Let R be any graded KLR datum in this page over any field k. For a finite-dimensional graded module M of weight beta set epsilon_i(M)=max{r:e(beta-r alpha_i,r alpha_i)M!=0}. If S is simple and r=epsilon_i(S)>0, there is a simple graded R(beta-r alpha_i)-module N with epsilon_i(N)=0 such that Delta_i^r S=N boxtimes L(i^r), where L(i^r) is the unique nil-Hecke simple up to shift. Conversely, for any such N, Ind(N boxtimes L(i^r)) has a unique simple graded head S, appearing once as a composition factor, with epsilon_i(S)=r and Delta_i^r S=N boxtimes L(i^r). Every other composition factor has smaller i-tail. The graded simples of every R(beta) remain simple without grading and are absolutely simple; all ordinary endomorphisms are k and nonzero homogeneous endomorphisms have degree0. The classes of normalized simples and their projective covers are therefore unscaled dual shift-orbit bases for the projective/simple Hom pairing. For each beta there is a finite family of ordered divided-power words Y_b whose normalized projective classes pair triangularly with the simple classes, with diagonal entries1 after choosing the simple grading shifts. Thus the selected [P(Y_b)] form an A-basis of K_0(R(beta)); arbitrary divided words span, but need not be a basis. The identical statements hold for maximal FIRST-color blocks, with epsilon_i^L(M)=max{r:e(r alpha_i,beta-r alpha_i)M!=0}, restriction Delta_i^(L,r), and induction Ind(L(i^r) boxtimes N).
